plants.name: Prunus mume
plants.description: Bare, dark branches burst into clusters of spicy-sweet, blush-pink blossoms. They open before any leaves appear, so the whole tree looks lit from within. Ume orchards and shrine gardens across Japan fill with fragrance while the weather is still cold.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late January through March, peaking in February
plants.location: Japan, including the plum groves and shrine gardens of Honshu
plants.funFact: Ume blooms weeks before cherry blossoms. In Japan and China it is a symbol of perseverance, because it flowers in the cold at the end of winter.

plants.name: Galanthus nivalis
plants.description: Small, nodding, bell-shaped white flowers hang from slender stems. Each has a green-tipped inner ring and sits above a clump of narrow, blue-green leaves. Snowdrops carpet woodlands and old churchyards, and they often push up through frost or a dusting of snow.
plants.bloomingSeason: January to March, with peak bloom in February
plants.location: Woodlands and gardens across the United Kingdom and temperate Europe
plants.funFact: Snowdrops make their own natural antifreeze-like proteins. Their leaves are tough enough to push through frozen ground. The plant is also the source of galantamine, a compound used in Alzheimer's medicine.

plants.name: Camellia japonica
plants.description: Glossy evergreen shrubs carry large, rose-like blooms of layered petals around golden stamens. The flowers appear when most other plants are dormant. In mild-winter regions such as the southeastern United States, camellias light up gardens from late winter into spring.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to early spring, February to April in many regions
plants.location: Gardens of the southeastern United States, and native to Japan, Korea and eastern Asia
plants.funFact: Camellia japonica belongs to the same genus as the tea plant, Camellia sinensis. Its seeds are pressed for camellia oil, a traditional hair and skin oil in Japan.
